name: South Steens Campground
note: BLM Burns District campground on the west side of Steens Mountain (Steens Mtn Cooperative Management Area). 36 family sites amid juniper/sage plus an adjacent 15-site equestrian loop with corrals; general campground, not equestrian-only. Vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups. Typically open mid-May through mid-November. Trailheads (Big Indian Gorge, Little Blitzen) at the campground. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Typically open mid-May to mid-November.
field_notes.Fees: BLM Burns District page (read 2026-11-07): $16 a night per vehicle, where one vehicle is a single car, truck, or RV with its towed vehicle; additional passenger vehicles $5 a night. First-come, first-served; pay cash or check at the kiosk.

name: Sixes River Campground
note: BLM Coos Bay District (Myrtlewood FO) campground along the Sixes River E of the coast at Sixes; gravel spurs fit rigs up to ~30 ft; popular for salmon fishing and gold panning; self-registration; open Fri before Memorial Day-Sept 30. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Open the Friday before Memorial Day to September 30.

name: Bear Wallow Creek Campground
note: Small Umatilla NF (North Fork John Day RD) camp on Bear Wallow Creek, ~11.5 mi E of Ukiah off Hwy 244. 8 gravel sites, vault toilets, no potable water/no garbage service; Open Memorial Day-mid Nov (snow closes access). --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Open Memorial Day to mid-November (snow closes access).

name: Drift Fence Campground
note: Small rustic Umatilla NF hunting camp along FR 52 (Blue Mountain Scenic Byway) S of Ukiah; 6 sites, 2 vault toilets, no potable water/no garbage. Short access road is rough but passable; open Memorial Day-mid Nov, closed only by snow. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Open Memorial Day to mid-November, closed only by snow.

name: Metzler Park
note: Clackamas County park on Clear Creek ~5 mi south of Estacada; 75 sites, 60 with water/electric hookups (sites 28-37 and 71-75 are tent-only), free hot showers, swim area, 2.5 mi of trails. Open May 1-Sep 30, reservable at least 3 days ahead (no minimum stay for a single site; Clackamas County camping rules, 2026-10-12). --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Reservations must be made at least 3 days ahead (up to a year); no minimum stay for a single site - the county's 2-night weekend minimum (July 1 - Labor Day) is for groups of 10+ sites (Clackamas County camping rules).
field_notes.Fees: Clackamas County: partial utility (water/electric) sites $42 a night, full utility $48.25; non-Oregon residents $52/$60; standard no-utility $31.75; $12.25 non-refundable reservation fee. Read 2026-10-16.

name: Eagle Valley RV Park
note: Small commercial RV park at 40254 OR-86 near Richland in the Eagle Valley (Pine Valley area of Baker County). 40 sites, ~25 pull-throughs, 25 full hookups (electric/water/sewer), big-rig friendly, showers, restrooms, laundry, fish-cleaning station. Reserve by phone. Camper-reported rate: $29 a night for full hookups (Campendium, May and July 2025). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Campendium reviewers paid $29 a night for full hookups in May and July 2025.

name: Wild Horse State Recreation Area
note: 34-site campground on a rise above Wild Horse Reservoir; pull-through sites accommodate large RVs, each with camp pad, shade and fire pit; Loop 2's sites have water and electric hookups (the booking site and Nevada State Parks' fee page, 2026-10-12), Loop 1's none; restrooms/showers year-round, dump station + water faucets in summer. Reservable via ReserveNevada. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: $15 per vehicle a night for Nevada vehicles, $20 for others, plus $10 at a site with utility hookups. Plus the $5 reservation transaction fee. On the booking site: Loop 1: sites without hookups; Loop 2: water and electric. Nevada State Parks' fees and reservations pages and ReserveNevada, read 2026-10-12.

name: Jarbidge Campground
note: Small primitive Humboldt-Toiyabe NF campground at the historic town of Jarbidge (~6,350 ft) in Jarbidge Canyon, NE Nevada; a handful of sites best for small/medium rigs (~22-24 ft, comparable to nearby Sawmill). Open ~June-Oct once the canyon road clears. Reached via the long graded Jarbidge Canyon Rd - remote but passable by a normal vehicle. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Open about June to October, once the canyon road clears.

name: White River Campground
note: Small rustic Humboldt-Toiyabe NF (Ely Ranger District) campground ~30 mi west of Ely, then 9.5 mi in on graded gravel NFSR-405. 5 dispersed-style sites along the White River with picnic tables and fire rings; vault toilet, no potable water, no hookups. Open roughly late May through mid-October. Reviewers note lots of flat ground; graded gravel access. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Open roughly late May to mid-October.

name: DeMotte Campground
note: Kaibab NF (North Kaibab RD), on AZ-67 ~7 mi N of the Grand Canyon North Rim entrance (~8,800 ft) beside DeMotte Park meadow. 38 single sites in two loops, limited potable water (no RV-tank fills). Half reservable via recreation.gov, half FCFS; mid-May-mid-Oct (road closed in winter). --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Mid-May to mid-October (road closed in winter).

name: FR 9350 Dispersed Camping
note: Apache-Sitgreaves NF designated dispersed camping along Forest Road 9350, a ~2-mi dirt spur off well-graded FR 300 (Rim Road) atop the Mogollon Rim near Heber. ~42 primitive marked sites spread over ~1.25 mi, many with rim views; two vault toilets near the Carr Lake trailhead, metal fire rings. Open roughly May-Nov (impassable after snowfall). Some sites sit near a ~200-ft rim drop-off. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Open roughly May to November (impassable after snowfall).

name: Rim Campground
note: Apache-Sitgreaves NF (Black Mesa RD) at the Mogollon Rim edge on FR-300, ~1 mi off SR-260, at ~7,540 ft; known for 100-mile rim views. 26 sites (1-13 FCFS, 14-26 reservable online). Woods Canyon Lake ~3 mi. Open ~mid-May through Labor Day weekend. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Open about mid-May through Labor Day weekend.

name: Molino Basin Campground
note: Coronado NF (Santa Catalina RD) campground at ~4,300 ft on the Catalina Hwy up Mt Lemmon, ~10 mi NE of Tucson. 37 sites off paved roads, 2WD/low-clearance accessible; no hookups, no potable water. Trailers/RVs listed to 22 ft (borderline for a 23-ft rig — a few of the larger sites fit). Open Nov 1–early May (low-elevation winter site). Reservable online. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Open November 1 to early May (winter site).

name: Lower Wolf Creek Campground
note: Prescott NF, on the banks of Wolf Creek south of Prescott. 20 CCC-built sites with tables and fire rings; no hookups, no drinking water, vault toilets. Open Memorial Day weekend through Oct 31. Sites accommodate trailers ~22-40 ft; graded-dirt/FR-97 access. (Temporarily closed for bear activity at time of research.) --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Open Memorial Day weekend through October 31.

name: Watson Lake Park
note: City of Prescott lakeside park in the Granite Dells on Watson Lake; 35 campsites (19 reservable, remainder first-come, first-served), tent/RV, restrooms, picnic table/fire pit/grill each site. Open ~1st weekend of April through 1st weekend of October, Thu-Mon nights only. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Open about the first weekend of April through the first weekend of October (Thu-Mon nights only).
field_notes.Fees: City of Prescott (Watson Lake): $25 a site a night. Read 2026-10-16.

name: Norma's RV Park
note: Small family-owned RV park on historic Route 66 in Joseph City, open year-round. ~30 sites, gravel level pull-throughs with full hookups (30/50 amp), water/sewer, dump station; geared to overnighters and short stays. Satellite shows a short RV row off Main St just north of I-40. Camper-reported rate: $40 a night in May 2026, $35 in August 2025 (Campendium). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Campendium reviewers paid $35 a night in August 2025 and $40 in May 2026.

name: Sunrise Park Campground and RV Park
note: Sunrise RV Park at the White Mountain Apache Tribe's Sunrise Park Resort in the White Mountains (~2810 m), off Hwy 273 near Sunrise Lake. 16 dry (no-hookup) drive-in tent/RV/trailer spots; potable water and port-a-johns throughout, tables and fire pits at most sites. Permits bought at the Sunrise General Store or Park Lodge (no online booking). Tribal land. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Sunrise Park: RV $35, tent $15; permits from the general store or lodge. Read 2026-10-15.

name: Snowbird West RV Park
note: Off-grid desert RV park at 50875 Ave 75 E, Salome (La Paz County), open Oct 1-Apr 30. ~40 large spread-out dry-camp sites, no on-site electric; water available limited afternoon hours, honey-wagon tank drainage, showers/laundry/restrooms. Takes daily overnighters as well as weekly/monthly/yearly snowbird stays; genuine drive-in transient RV camping. Camper-reported rate: $25 a night from 2025 (Campendium, January 2025). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: A Campendium reviewer reported in January 2025 that the daily rate went up to $25 a night ($100 a week, $200 a month) for 2025.

name: Catalina State Park
note: Arizona State Parks & Trails campground at the base of the Santa Catalina Mountains north of Tucson. 120 sites (Loops A and B) with 20/30/50-amp electric and water; no length limit on RVs. Reservable online. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Campgrounds A and B: every site has 20/30/50-amp electric and water, $50 a night. Ringtail Campground (overflow, no hookups) is $25, open January 1 to March 31 only. Plus the $3.60 reservation fee; a second vehicle is $15 a night. Park entry included. Arizona State Parks' fee schedule and the park's camping page, read 2026-10-12.

name: Patagonia Lake State Park
note: Arizona State Parks & Trails, on 265-acre Patagonia Lake in the Santa Rita foothills. Over 100 developed campsites incl. RV sites with water/electric hookups plus boat-in sites; reservable online. Standard drive-in loops fit a 23-ft rig. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Electric and water sites $50 a night; the 2 non-electric sites ($25) are 22 ft long for campers and trailers; boat-in sites $25. Plus the $3.60 reservation fee; a second vehicle is $15 a night. Park entry included. Arizona State Parks' fee schedule and the park's camping page, read 2026-10-12.

name: Boggs Mountain Demonstration State Forest - Calso Camp
note: CAL FIRE demonstration state forest (Cobb/Middletown). Calso Camp is the forest's only non-group campground: 14 rustic sites, self-issue camping permit from CAL FIRE; no running water (bring your own). Small trailers/RVs allowed if they fit the site. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: CAL FIRE's fee at Boggs Mountain Demonstration State Forest: $25 a day for a designated camping area, two vehicles included, paid on arrival; first come, first served (14 CCR § 1401.1, operative 2021-04-01; read 2026-10-12).

name: Agua Caliente County Park
note: San Diego County desert park in the Anza-Borrego area with natural hot springs. ~140 sites across several loops: full-hookup, partial-hookup, and no-hookup RV/trailer sites plus tent sites; flush toilets, showers, dump station. Seasonally operated (open ~Labor Day to Memorial Day; closed summer heat). Reservable online through San Diego County Parks. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Open about Labor Day to Memorial Day (closed in summer heat).

name: Del Mar Fairgrounds RV Park
note: Two RV lots on the Del Mar Fairgrounds (22nd District Agricultural Association), minutes from the beach: Surf & Turf RV Park (60 sites) and the fairgrounds' own RV lot (58 spaces), all back-in with full hookups.  Restrooms and laundry.  Daily and weekly stays, booked up to 2 months ahead, 21 nights a calendar year at most.  Closed in summer for the San Diego County Fair and the racing season. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Book up to 2 months ahead; 21 nights a calendar year at most.
field_notes.Fees: Read on CampLife: one night, site rate before tax, every RV site a 23-ft rig fits (Back In). October 2026: $67-85, Tuesday and Saturday alike. January 2027 and June 2027 aren't open for booking yet. An online booking adds $3.50 once a stay. Read 2026-10-14.

name: Rocky Point Campground (Lake Almanor)
note: PG&E-operated campground on the wooded west shore of Lake Almanor (Rocky Point peninsula near Canyon Dam); ~130 drive-in forest sites, sandy beach/day-use nearby. --Claude  Reservations need at least 2 nights; first-come, first-served sites can be taken for one night (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Reservations need at least 2 nights (max 14) and can't be made within 3 days of arrival; reservations for the season open April 15. Some sites are first-come, first-served, and those can be taken for a single night. Kept per AWH 2026-10-10: the FCFS sites mean a one-night stay is possible.
field_notes.Fees: PG&E reservation site, July 6-8 2027 search (2-night 'Use Fee' halved; 3-night check at Lake McCumber confirmed it is the stay total). $30/night; double sites $60. Other fees and taxes may apply; cancellation $15 per site.

name: Ponderosa Flat Campground (Butt Valley Reservoir)
note: PG&E utility-operated campground on the east shore of Butt Valley Reservoir (Butt Lake) near Canyondam; ~63 drive-in sites, boat ramp and swim beach. First-come, first-served. --Claude  Road work on Butt-Prattville Road near Cool Springs, Ray Adams Boat Launch and Ponderosa Flat from Aug 10, 2026 through the rest of the 2026 season: traffic delays, heavy trucks, noise and dust (PG&E notice, 2026-10-10). --Claude  Reservations need at least 2 nights; first-come, first-served sites can be taken for one night (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Reservations need at least 2 nights (max 14) and can't be made within 3 days of arrival; reservations for the season open April 15. Some sites are first-come, first-served, and those can be taken for a single night. Kept per AWH 2026-10-10: the FCFS sites mean a one-night stay is possible.
field_notes.Fees: PG&E reservation site, July 6-8 2027 search (2-night 'Use Fee' halved; 3-night check at Lake McCumber confirmed it is the stay total). $30/night; double sites $60, group pods $90-180. Other fees and taxes may apply; cancellation $15 per site.
